figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Two coupled SMTJs, modeled as two Ising spins S1 and S2, with interaction strengths J1←2 and J2←1, as well as finite time delays t1←2 and t2←1. Experimental auto- and cross-correlation data are shown in (b) and (c) respectively, with maximum coupling strength allowed by the circuit and J1←2 ≈ −J2←1. Results from simulations with anti-symmetric coupling, for instantaneous interactions is shown in (d,e) and time-delayed interactions in (f,g) for the auto-correlation function (d,f) and for the cross-correlation function (e,g) as a function of tlag, the time difference between measurements of digitized SMTJ voltage states or spin states. The intrinsic characteristic time scale of each spin in the model is τ = 1/λ0 flip. 95 % confidence intervals of correlation functions are obtained from standard statistical analysis but are narrower than the width of the line. Simulations are performed with τ = 4.98 ∆t, ∆Ei = 4 kT , J1←2 = −J2←1 = kT , h1 = h2 = 0, t1←2 = t2←1 = 0 for (d) and (e) or t1←2 = t2←1 = 100 ∆t for (f) and (g). Each data point gives the mean correlation averaged over 104 ensembles and for 5000 ∆t after reaching steady state. Details of simulation parameters are given in Section III.

FIG. 3. Evolution of probability distribution of ferromagnetically coupled spins (J1←2 = J2←1 > 0), where initial states are ↓↓ for t ≤ 0, with long time delay and without time delay shown in (a,b), respectively. In (c,d), two spins initially evolve without time delay and with constant J1←2(t) = J2←1(t) = kT in (c) or linearly increasing J1←2(t) = J2←1(t) = kT t/2510τ in (d) until t = 2510τ (indicated by the dashed line). After that, two spins evolve with long time delay and constant J1←2(t) = J2←1(t) = kT . t is the evolving time. Steady-state distribution of spin states, reflected by Rlog, as a function of time delay t1←2 and t2←1 with ferromagnetic and anti-symmetric coupling (J1←2 = −J2←1 > 0) shown in (e,f), respectively. The color bar and height of the surface correspond to Rlog. Black dashed line in (f) corresponds to t1←2 = t2←1. τ = 1/λ0 flip is the intrinsic characteristic time scale of each spin in (a)(f). Simulations are performed with τ = 4.98∆t, ∆Ei = 4kT , |J1←2| = |J2←1| = kT , h1 = h2 = 0, t1←2 = t2←1 = 5000∆t for (a) and for t > 2510τ in (c,d), and t1←2 = t2←1 = 0 for (b) and for t < 2510τ in (c,d). Each data point gives the mean value averaged over 104 ensembles for (a)-(f), 5000∆t period of time for (e,f) after reaching steady state. 95 % confidence intervals of probabilities and Rlog are obtained from standard statistical analysis but are narrower than the width of the line, for example, the 95 % confidence interval for Rlog is ±0.057.

FIG. 4. Probability distributions in the presence of bias and time delay. Spins are coupled with symmetric coupling in (a,b), or with anti-symmetric coupling in (c,d). There exists time delay t1←2 = t2←1 = 500∆t in (a,c), or there is no time delay t1←2 = t2←1 = 0 in (b,d). Bias is h1 = h2 = kT in (a)-(d). Overlapped lines are slightly shifted for visual clarity. Simulations are performed with τ = 4.98∆t, ∆Ei = 4kT . Each data point gives the mean value averaged over 104 ensembles and 5000∆t period of time after reaching steady state. 95 % confidence intervals of log10(Pα) obtained from standard statistical analysis are plotted as shaded regions.

FIG. 6. Entropy of five coupled spins. (a) evolution of entropy with respect to time, t, of 5 ferromagnetically coupled spins (Ji←j = Jj←i = 0.2kT ), where initial states are Si = −1, with long time delay and without time delay. (b) Dependence of entropy of 5 ferromagnetically (Ji←j = Jj←i = 0.2kT ) and anti-symmetrically (Ji←j = −Jj←i = 0.2kT ) coupled spins on the time delay ti←j . Entropy dependence on the coupling strengths in the presence of bias is shown in (c) for symmetric coupling and (d) for anti-symmetric coupling. In (a)-(d), black dashed lines correspond to the maximum possible entropy of 5 ln 2, and ti←j = tj←i. τ = 1/λ0 flip is the intrinsic characteristic time scale of each spin in (a,b). Simulations are performed with τ = 4.98∆t, ∆Ei = 4kT , hi = 0 for (a,b), hi = 0.2kT for (c,d), ti←j = 104∆t for (a) and ti←j = 500∆t for (c,d). Each data point gives the mean value averaged over 104 ensembles, 5000∆t period of time for (b)(d) after reaching steady state. 95 % confidence intervals of entropy obtained from standard statistical analysis are plotted as shaded regions.

FIG. 7. Correlation functions of five coupled spins with nonzero time delay and without time delay. Spins are coupled ferromagnetically in (a,b), and anti-symmetrically in (c,d). Auto- and cross-correlation functions are shown in (a,c) and (b,d), respectively. tlag is the time difference between two measurements of spin states and τ = 1/λ0 flip is the intrinsic characteristic time scale of each spin. Simulations are performed with τ = 4.98∆t, ∆Ei = 4kT , ti←j = tj←i = 200∆t for ti←j ̸= 0 lines. Each data point gives the mean value averaged over 104 ensembles and 1250∆t period of time after reaching steady state. 95 % confidence intervals of correlation functions obtained from standard statistical analysis are plotted as shaded regions.

FIG. 8. Steady-state probability distribution dependence on J1←2 and J2←1 with long time delay. There are non-zero biases h1 = h2 = kT . Simulations are performed with τ = 4.98∆t, ∆Ei = 4kT , t1←2 = t2←1 = 500∆t. Each data point gives the mean value averaged over 104 ensembles and 5000∆t period of time after reaching steady state. 95 % confidence intervals of probabilities obtained from standard statistical analysis are plotted as envelop.

FIG. 9. Steady-state probability distribution dependence on h1 and h2 with long time delay. Spins are coupled ferromagnetically (J1←2 = J2←1 = kT ). Simulations are performed with τ = 4.98∆t, ∆Ei = 4kT , t1←2 = t2←1 = 500∆t. Each data point gives the mean value averaged over 104 ensembles and 5000∆t period of time after reaching steady state. 95 % confidence intervals of probabilities obtained from standard statistical analysis are plotted as envelopes.

FIG. 10. Steady-state probability distribution dependence on h1 and h2 with long time delay. Spins are uncoupled (J1←2 = J2←1 = 0). Simulations are performed with τ = 4.98∆t, ∆Ei = 4kT , t1←2 = t2←1 = 500∆t. Each data point gives the mean value averaged over 104 ensembles and 5000∆t period of time after reaching steady state. 95 % confidence intervals of probabilities obtained from standard statistical analysis are plotted as envelopes.

FIG. 11. Experimental auto- (ρauto) and cross- (ρcross) correlation functions with varying coupling strengths. The coupling between two SMTJs are fully anti-symmetric, and the coupling strength is 0 in (a,b), 0.5 Jmax in (c,d), and Jmax in (e,f). Jmax is the maximum possible coupling allowed by the circuit. tlag is the time difference between two measurements of digitized SMTJ voltage states. 95 % confidence intervals of correlation functions obtained from standard statistical analysis are plotted as envelopes.
